analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: The SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions, the biggest 9-day stretch of underperformance in 20+ years. The SOX is now testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025.
The NDX lagged the NDX equal-weight index by about 138 bps on the prior day, a bottom-5 day in more than 10 years.

GS Credit Tracker: credit investors face cost of capital concerns, a multi-year AI-related financing wave, and positioning and year-to-date performance dynamics, which may be worsening the recent risk-off moves.
GS had flagged the March 2026 spread peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY) as the downside-scenario base case. Spreads are close to those levels and GS now expects them to moderately overshoot.

Strategic M&A is tracking at year-to-date records in North America and Europe, led by Technology and Financials, with large deals especially active. Financing has become somewhat more bondholder friendly, but USD M&A-related debt issuance is still elevated. GS expects EUR M&A-related debt supply to rise from a low base.

Sponsor-related deals remain muted because higher rates hurt valuations and have delayed private equity exits. The pressure is greatest for 2020-2021 vintages, which were underwritten at low rates and before AI disruption risk to legacy software was priced in.

Spotify Q3: management stressed strong premium subscriber growth with a broader set of geographies, advertising heading toward double-digit revenue growth, and monetization broadening across pricing, add-ons and new subscription products. GS says management treats AI, cloud and product investment as transient, which raises GS conviction in gross and operating margin progression in 2027.

Spotify management framed the agentic media platform as an opportunity, with a rising role for content discovery through its Large Taste model. This countered investor fears of disintermediation. Capital returns were a positive in the quarter.

Nvidia GTC Berlin takeaways: GS expects little immediate stock impact but sees AI deployments on track. Customers including hyperscalers and neoclouds are getting strong unit economics from datacenter deployments, Nvidia is offering hardware and software to secure enterprise AI agents, and physical AI revenue is growing quickly. GS maintains Buy.

Deckers F2Q: EPS of $2.31 included a $0.28 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit, and ex-benefit EPS of $2.03 beat GS/FactSet consensus of $1.77/$1.80. Sales were weaker than expected at both HOKA and UGG, and management cut its FY sales outlook for both brands.

Deckers management blamed a roughly $22mn EMEA 3PL shipment delay and slower US growth from athletic footwear industry weakness and more muted consumer behaviour, which hit US e-commerce. HOKA is guided weak near term with reacceleration weighted to 4Q and FY28. GS calls the update disappointing and expects profitability to be in focus in FY28 as DECK cycles the tariff refund benefit in the FY27 guide.

Market update: risk assets were under pressure, with the US 10Y down 15 bps to 4.97%, the largest 1-day move of the year. Oil is back at YTD highs on escalating Middle East tensions, and META, TSLA, LRCX and IBM did not give the market enough to rally.

GS PB saw Fundamental L/S down 1.1%, Systematics down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4% by midday, the first time since Covid that all three fell more than 1% on the same day. The GS HF Positioning Pair fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% MTD.

The desk sees the AI-driven selloff pushing investors to reassess long-term growth expectations, with NDX closely correlated to US 10Y yields. The 10Y closed below the CTA short-term threshold, which the desk expects to bring more bond demand in tomorrow's flow estimates. The desk is watching for spillover from European rates overnight.

The bull case for the week was that tech earnings would stabilize the tape. Wednesday's reactions were constructive, but META and LRCX failed to continue that today. WDC reports tonight (+2% after hours) ahead of a busy week of megacap earnings.

The GS AI basket is down 23% from its June highs, a similar drawdown to the one before the July bounce. High Beta Momentum has erased all of its YTD gains, driven by the AI-correlated long leg, and GS notes that similar momentum drawdowns have historically been attractive entry points. SPX ex-AI has outperformed the S&P by 6% MTD.

Flows: the desk saw no offensive buying around the AI theme and little rotation out of AI despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and parts of Financials. The floor finished 9.6% better for sale, Asset Managers about 20% better for sale on large-cap tech and ETF supply, and Hedge Funds 10% better for sale on semis and hardware supply plus ETF shorting. Floor activity was a 5 out of 10.

Dispersion was high: 155 S&P names moved 2.0 standard deviations or more, the most since May 2025, while 335 S&P names finished higher. That is one of the widest gaps between S&P breadth and index performance since the 1990s.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy after Jensen Huang's GTC Berlin keynote and sees a positive catalyst path from greater AI datacenter deployment visibility and capital returns of about $235bn in authorized buybacks.
F2Q EPS beat consensus, but sales missed at HOKA and UGG and FY sales guidance was cut. GS calls the update disappointing and flags US footwear pressure and FY28 profitability as the focus.
GS says the Q3 review raised its conviction that 2027 will bring further gross and operating margin progression, with strong premium subscriber growth and broadening monetization.

earnings_insights: Deckers F2Q: reported EPS $2.31 including a $0.28 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit. Ex-benefit EPS $2.03 vs GS consensus $1.77 and FactSet consensus $1.80. Sales were below expectations at both brands and FY sales outlook was lowered for HOKA and UGG.

Spotify Q3 (reported): premium subscriber growth strong, advertising trending toward double-digit revenue growth in Q3'26, and management was optimistic on Q4 revenue. GS does not raise 2027 estimates but raises conviction on 2027 margin progression.
Nvidia: 1HFY27 physical AI revenue of $11B is well ahead of all of FY26. About $235bn in buybacks are authorized.
WDC reports tonight and was up 2% after hours. Megacap earnings follow next week.
Reporting pre-market on 23 Oct: AXP, E, SLB, INFY, FCNCA, RCI. No post-market reports listed.
